notes._summary: CommonMark 0.31.2 baseline measured against Supramark's DEFAULT parser config (issue #144 premise). The default config ships the GFM bare-URL/email autolink extension ON, so bare `https://`, `www.` and `foo@bar` are linkified. CommonMark 0.31.2 has no such extension — its Autolinks section expects bare URLs/emails to stay literal — so the 4 cases listed here diverge. These are legitimate GFM-vs-CommonMark spec differences, not parser bugs: 0602 (`<https://foo.bar/baz bim>`, invalid bracketed autolink whose inner bare URL supramark linkifies), 0608 (`< https://foo.bar >`, same), 0611 (`https://example.com` bare URL), 0612 (`foo@bar.example.com` bare email). They are baselined rather than hidden: the gate parses every case with the default config and surfaces these as expected divergences. The parallel cmark-gfm spec-* Autolinks cases (spec-0610/0616/0619/0620) carry the same caveat in baselines/cmark-gfm.json.
notes.commonmark-0.31.2-0602: Autolinks: DIVERGENCE — CommonMark expects the invalid bracketed autolink `<https://foo.bar/baz bim>` to render literal (`<…>`); Supramark's default config (GFM autolink on) linkifies the bare `https://foo.bar/baz` inside. Legitimate GFM-vs-CommonMark difference, baselined.
notes.commonmark-0.31.2-0608: Autolinks: DIVERGENCE — `< https://foo.bar >` expected literal; Supramark default linkifies the bare `https://foo.bar`. Legitimate GFM-vs-CommonMark difference, baselined.
notes.commonmark-0.31.2-0611: Autolinks: DIVERGENCE — bare `https://example.com` expected literal; Supramark default (GFM autolink on) linkifies it. Legitimate GFM-vs-CommonMark difference, baselined.
notes.commonmark-0.31.2-0612: Autolinks: DIVERGENCE — bare `foo@bar.example.com` expected literal; Supramark default (GFM autolink on) linkifies it as a mailto. Legitimate GFM-vs-CommonMark difference, baselined.
